MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md shows Stage 6 (guest comments) is the only stage not built. Both its prerequisites are discharged (rate limiter, Slice 62; RawHtmlContractTests, Slice 63).

A finding I found while reading for it — worth flagging now
§19's M7 bullet still says Stage 6 is "recorded as not startable until §17's rate-limit ruling is revisited." It was revisited eleven slices ago. Worse, §17 carries two accounts of the same mechanism: the corrected one ("The mechanism, kept because…"), and then, four paragraphs below it, the pre-fix version in future tense — "When it lands, §13 gains the window and permit count beside DISPLAY_PAIRING_*." §13 already has them. That's F-114's rule violated exactly: a correction sitting above the claim it corrects instead of replacing it. And §17 says "the habit that follows … is stated in §18" — §18 does not state it.

That's F-122, three limbs, remedy is deletion rather than correction.

The slice I had planned (Slice 68 — Stage 6c: schema and data access)
Design settled against existing rulings: comment attached to the item, not an order line (§7's like ruling already decided an opinion needs no prior order); staff-facing, guest sees only their own (§11.4's like-count rule — which dissolves the moderation question); one standing comment per person per dish, editing appends, withdrawal is a withdrawn event and the text stays in the log (F-10b, §6.7); cap lives only in the CHECK constraint, read back via pg_get_constraintdef (F-107's "the number travels"). Files: 0009_menu_item_comments.sql, Menu/MenuItemComments.cs, MenuItemCommentTests.cs (12 facts), plus edits to OrdersServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, MenuWiringTests.cs (29→30), SchemaMigrationRunnerTests.cs (two relations), and all five documents. Presented file
Slice 68 — Stage 6c: guest comments, the schema and the data access. Extract at the repository root; all eleven paths are repo-relative and complete files.

tar xzf myrestaurant-slice-68.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
Three files need git add (invisible to every git ls-files gate until you do):

src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Migrations/0009_menu_item_comments.sql
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Menu/MenuItemComments.cs
tests/MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tests/Menu/MenuItemCommentTests.cs
Nothing to delete. The csproj glob already picks up the migration.

Expected: 1320 tests. 1304 + 13 + 1 + 2 (the two extra KeyRelations rows expand a [MemberData] theory, so §16.4's seven for SchemaMigrationRunnerTests doesn't move).

Three of Stage 6's four open questions are ruled in §7: filed against the item, never an order line; staff-facing, a guest sees only their own — which makes the moderation question not arise rather than answered; one standing comment per person per dish, editing is resubmission, withdrawal is an event, every version kept. Staff replies stay deferred and are named as deferred.

Two schema decisions are rulings rather than shape, and both are in §8.2/§8.3 with their reasons. The fold has no WHERE clause — DISTINCT ON must see the withdrawal to know it's the latest row, so filtering inside the view would report a withdrawn comment as standing. And there are four separately named constraints over one nullable column rather than one conjunction, because the writer recognises the cap refusal by conname and a conjunction would make over-cap and blank indistinguishable to the code that has to tell a guest which happened.

F-122, found by reading §19 to decide what to build. §19 said Stage 6 was not startable until §17's rate-limit ruling was revisited — revisited in Slice 62. §17 was worse: the corrected account of the limiter, then four paragraphs below it the pre-fix account in future tense, promising §13 gains variables it's had since v1.47. And §17 claimed the habit F-115 produced is stated in §18 — §18 didn't state it. All three are deletions or replacements on F-114's ruling; §18 now carries the habit. No gate holds this, and that's recorded as a residual with its reason: catching a stale promise means reading prose for a tense, which F-116 and F-119 forbid.

Gates emulated green against the edited tree: census 46/floor 37, version 1.53 matching newest entry, four named vocabularies agreeing spec↔migration in both directions, Markdown tables clean, byte hygiene clean on all ten files, no comments in authored source.

Four veto points are in _CHANGES.md with reversion instructions — the most consequential being the one-comment-per-person partition, since reversing it later is a new migration rather than an edit to 0009.

Nothing was compiled and nothing ran; no SDK and no container engine here. The full "what was NOT verified" is in _CHANGES.md and BUILD_PROGRESS.md.
